official.deadline_note: Consortium deadline only: the MSCA '6 steps' guidance gives 24 November 2026, 17.00 CET, via the Funding and Tenders Portal. Individual doctoral candidates are not bound by this call - they apply to vacancies advertised by projects that win funding.
official.application_cycle: 2026 call HORIZON-MSCA-2026-DN-01 (opened 28 May 2026; notification April 2027; grant agreements July 2027; projects start September 2027)
official.status_note: The 2026 call opened on 28 May 2026 and closes 24 November 2026; REA lists EUR 593.03 million overall indicative budget for the call, funding over 130 projects and around 1,950 doctoral candidates.
official.funding_period: per month (gross living allowance, before CCC)
benefits: Living allowance: EUR 4,250 per person-month, a gross amount before the country correction coefficient is applied
Mobility allowance: EUR 710 per person-month, covering additional private mobility-related costs such as travel and accommodation
Family allowance: EUR 660 per person-month if the researcher has or acquires family obligations during the action
Long-term leave allowance: EUR 4,960 x % covered by the beneficiary (if applicable)
Special needs allowance: requested unit x (1/number of months) (if applicable)
Research, training and networking contribution: EUR 1,600 per person-month; management and indirect contribution: EUR 1,200 per person-month
eligibility: Consortium: at least three independent legal entities, each established in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country, with at least one established in an EU Member State
Other organisations from any country in the world may join on top of the minimum, as beneficiaries or associated partners
All beneficiaries must recruit at least one doctoral candidate and host/supervise them at their premises or via linked associated partners
Not more than 40% of the EU contribution may be allocated to beneficiaries in the same country or to a single international organisation
Recruited researcher: must not have a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment (a defended but not yet awarded thesis still counts as eligible)

Recruited researcher: any nationality, but must comply with the mobility rule - no more than 12 months of residence or main activity in the country of the recruiting organisation in the 36 months immediately before recruitment
Recruited researcher: must be enrolled in a doctoral programme leading to a doctoral degree in at least one EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country
Industrial Doctorates: doctoral candidates must spend at least 50% of the fellowship duration in the non-academic sector
Joint Doctorates: at least three independent legal entities entitled to award doctoral degrees, with a joint governance structure covering admission, selection, supervision, monitoring and assessment
Researchers with refugee status under the Geneva Convention or beneficiaries of EU temporary protection are exempt from the mobility rule
requirements: Applications must be submitted by the consortium through the EU Funding and Tenders Portal (Electronic Submission Service)
Page limit of the application is 30 pages, excluding annexes
All proposals must indicate whether they are a resubmission from the previous MSCA Doctoral Networks call
Proposals that scored below 80% in the previous call must not be resubmitted the following year
Affiliated entities are not allowed to participate as they cannot claim costs in MSCA Doctoral Networks
documents: Consortium application: proposal and annexes submitted via the Funding and Tenders Portal, using the call's own proposal templates and application/evaluation forms
Consortium application: registered participant identification code (PIC) for each participating organisation
Doctoral candidates: documents are set by each funded project's vacancy advertisement; vacancies are published internationally, including on the EURAXESS jobs portal
selection_criteria: Award criteria: excellence, impact, and quality and efficiency of the implementation, each scored out of 5 with a threshold of 3
Weighting: excellence 50%, impact 30%, quality and efficiency of the implementation 20%
Proposals scoring equal to or above 70% are considered for funding within the limits of the available call budget
Quality and novelty of the research and innovation methodologies applied
Training, supervision and career guidance provided to researchers
Quality of supervision, with mandatory joint supervision for Industrial and Joint Doctorate projects
coverage: A living allowance, paid as a gross amount including compulsory deductions under national law such as employer and employee social security contributions and direct taxes
A mobility allowance covering the researcher's additional private mobility-related costs, for example travel and accommodation
If applicable, family, long-term leave and special needs allowances

Funding for research, training and networking activities, including conference participation, trips related to the action, training, language courses, lab material, books, publication costs, visa-related fees and travel expenses
Funding for management and indirect costs of the beneficiaries
Secondments for doctoral candidates anywhere in the world, and a career development plan agreed with the supervisor
application_method: Consortia apply through the Funding and Tenders Opportunities Portal, where the call page hosts the work programme, general annexes, guide for applicants, FAQs and forms
Consortia must register participating organisations and obtain PIC numbers before submitting
Doctoral candidates apply directly to the institution or project of their choice against advertised vacancies on EURAXESS, which lists the full requirements of each position
official.application_route: Consortia submit one coordinated proposal via the EU Funding and Tenders Portal; doctoral candidates apply to vacancies advertised by funded networks on EURAXESS.
official.study_mode: full-time; part-time is possible only for personal or family reasons, at least 50% of full working time, with prior approval of the granting authority
official.citizenship_residency: Any nationality for the recruited researcher, subject to the mobility rule; consortium members must be established in EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries
official.international_eligibility: Yes - any nationality for recruited researchers, subject to the mobility rule; organisations from any country in the world may join a consortium
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All areas of research may be funded, chosen freely by the applicants
official.research_requirement: Candidates must be enrolled in a doctoral programme during the project; networks must provide research training, transferable skills and (for Industrial and Joint Doctorates) joint supervision
official.duration: Doctoral Networks up to 4 years (up to 5 years for Joint Doctorate projects); each fellowship is between 3 and 36 months, or 3 and 48 months for Joint Doctorate fellowships; the overall EU contribution is limited to a maximum of 540 person-months
official.description: The objective of Doctoral Networks is to implement doctoral programmes by partnerships of organisations from different sectors across Europe and beyond to train highly skilled doctoral candidates, stimulate their creativity, enhance their innovation capacities and boost their employability in the long-term.
official.region: Europe (EU Member States and Horizon Europe Associated Countries)
official.program_type: Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions doctoral training programme, managed by the European Research Executive Agency

not_confirmed: tuition_coverage (the official pages publish no statement on tuition fees, so it is left null)
english_requirement (the official Doctoral Networks pages publish no English language requirement)
documents required from individual doctoral candidates (each project's own vacancy advertisement sets these)
verification.notes: Unit contributions (living allowance EUR 4,250/month gross before the country correction coefficient, mobility EUR 710, family EUR 660, research/training/networking EUR 1,600, management and indirect EUR 1,200) were read from page 70 of the official MSCA Work Programme 2026-2027 PDF on the ec.europa.eu domain; call dates, eligibility and award criteria from the MSCA and REA pages.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a scholarship you apply for directly: a consortium of at least three organisations from different EU Member States or Associated Countries wins the grant, then advertises PhD vacancies that you apply for on EURAXESS. Your money is a gross monthly living allowance of EUR 4,250 before the host country's correction coefficient, plus a EUR 710 mobility allowance, so your actual take-home depends on the host country's tax and social security system. The rule that rules most people out is the mobility rule: you cannot have spent more than 12 months in the host country in the three years before recruitment.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's graduates who already have a clear research idea and can show they have not been living in the country of their intended host.
application_readiness_checklist: Search EURAXESS for open MSCA-funded vacancies daily and set up alerts; networks advertise as soon as grant agreements are signed (July 2027 for the 2026 call)
Map your last 36 months of residence and main activity against the 12-month mobility rule before you invest time in any application
Confirm the host is a beneficiary of a funded network and that the position is funded as a Doctoral Network, not a self-funded PhD studentship
Prepare a concise research profile that connects your master's work to the network's stated topic, and check the vacancy's own required document list
Check whether the position is a standard, Industrial (50% outside academia) or Joint (joint/multiple degree) doctorate, since the contract, duration and degree outcome differ
common_rejection_risks: Failing the mobility rule because of a previous master's, internship or job in the host country - compulsory national service, holidays, refugee-status processing and EU temporary protection time are not counted
Already holding a doctoral degree, including a defended thesis that has not yet been formally awarded
Applying to a vacancy that is not part of a funded Doctoral Networks project
For consortia: proposing a network with fewer than three entities in different Member States or Associated Countries, or with more than 40% of the EU contribution in one country
For consortia: resubmitting a proposal that scored below 80% in the previous call, which is explicitly barred
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The living allowance is a gross figure including compulsory deductions under national law, so taxes and social security reduce the net pay, and the mobility allowance covers private mobility costs rather than relocation beyond that. Anything a host institution charges separately, plus costs for accompanying family members, are not covered by the published unit contributions.
document_audit: The candidate document list lives in each project's own vacancy advertisement, not in the call documents - read the specific vacancy rather than assuming a standard pack
The mobility rule is assessed against the recruitment date, so keep evidence of your residence and activity history for the 36 months before it
Consortia must flag resubmissions explicitly; 70% or more overlap in recruiting organisations with a previously unsuccessful proposal is assessed by evaluators regardless of self-declaration
alerts: The 24 November 2026 deadline applies to consortia; individual candidates apply whenever a network advertises, which is usually after grant signature in July 2027 for this call
The living allowance varies by country through the correction coefficient, so the same position pays different amounts in different countries
No application fee exists anywhere in this scheme - be suspicious of anyone charging you to place a PhD candidate in an MSCA network
Part-time working is only permitted for personal or family reasons and needs prior approval, so do not plan to hold another job alongside the fellowship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Consortium coordinator registers partners and submits one proposal in the Funding and Tenders Portal; candidates instead apply through the link in each EURAXESS vacancy and are recruited by the individual beneficiary.

official.deadline_note: There is no single central deadline: the official application timeline page instructs applicants to 'refer to your country page for the deadline' and notes the closing time is 11:00 UTC. As of 10 October 2026 Austria's country page read 'Open for applications until 20 October 2026, at 11:00 (UTC)' while India's read 'Applications for 2027-2028 Chevening Scholarships are now closed'.
official.status_note: As of 10 October 2026 most country/territory pages state that applications for 2027-2028 Chevening Scholarships are now closed; a few country pages (for example Austria) were still open until 20 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC. The next cycle is expected to open in August 2027.
benefits: Economy travel to and from your country of residence by an approved route for you only
The cost of an entry clearance (visa) application for you only

A monthly personal living allowance (stipend) to cover accommodation and living expenses; the stipend depends on whether you are studying inside or outside London and these rates are subject to annual review
eligibility: Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory
If applying for an award from an ODA-eligible country, be resident in an ODA-eligible country; all applicants must show a clear intention to support their country of award
Commit to returning to your home country (country of award) for at least two years after your scholarship ends
Have at least two years' work experience, acquired after completing your undergraduate degree, equivalent to 2,800 hours
Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme, finished at least two years before the application deadline
Apply to three different and eligible UK university courses and hold an unconditional offer from at least one by the deadline

Not eligible: holders of British or dual British citizenship, applicants resident in the UK at the time of application (excluding British Overseas Territories), and employees, immediate relatives or former employees (within the last two years from the opening of applications) of a government department, the British Council, a partner UK university or their wholly owned subsidiaries
Not eligible: applicants who have previously studied in the UK on a UK government-funded scholarship, and applicants holding refugee status in a country not eligible for Chevening
requirements: All applications must be completed via the online application system, accessed through the 'apply today' link on your country or territory page
Complete the online registration form, pass the eligibility checker, note your unique access code, complete each section of the application form, then submit
The application form must be completed in English; applications not completed in English are deemed ineligible
Applicants must submit their own original work - using AI software to generate answers is strictly prohibited and detected by Chevening's fraud, plagiarism and AI-content tools
Provide the names and contact details of two referees, who cannot be friends or relatives
Applying is free; Chevening does not endorse or work with third parties who charge for application support or advice
documents: No documents are required to be uploaded in order to submit an application
If selected for interview: photo ID
If selected for interview: the official undergraduate degree certificate issued by your university (originals required, transcripts are not accepted, no English translation needed)

If selected for interview: two reference letters in English, addressed to the British embassy or high commission in your country or territory, uploaded at least seven working days before the interview (or submitted directly to the local Chevening team)
If successful at interview: an unconditional offer from at least one of your three chosen UK university courses
selection_criteria: Applications are sifted against eligibility criteria, then assessed by independent reading committees (mid-October 2026 to January 2027 for this cycle)
Leadership and influencing skills, with concrete examples
The ability to build and maintain professional relationships to achieve positive outcomes

How the chosen course gives the skills to address pressing challenges linked to UK priority areas: promoting growth and prosperity, building resilience in a climate-vulnerable world, strengthening security and stability in a volatile world, and supporting development for more inclusive and effective societies
A realistic and achievable career plan for creating lasting positive change in your home country
Interview with panels at British embassies and high commissions, conducted in English
coverage: A monthly personal living allowance (stipend) to cover accommodation and living expenses, with different rates inside and outside London
Economy travel to and from your country of residence by an approved route, for the scholar only
An arrival allowance and a departure allowance
The cost of an entry clearance (visa) application for the scholar only, plus a contribution of up to £75 for TB testing where this is required
application_method: Open the online application system through the 'apply today' link on your country or territory page during the application window
Register, pass the eligibility checker, and record your unique access code
Complete and submit the application form, choosing three different eligible UK master's courses
Apply to your university courses as soon as possible after submitting your Chevening application
If invited to interview, upload your documents at least seven working days beforehand, then secure an unconditional offer
official.application_route: Apply through the online application system via your country/territory page, then interview at a British embassy or high commission and confirm an unconditional UK university offer.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory; you must apply from your country of citizenship regardless of where you currently live; applicants resident in the UK at the time of application are not eligible; ODA-eligible country applicants must be resident in an ODA-eligible country
official.international_eligibility: Yes - Chevening is designed for citizens of eligible countries and territories worldwide to study in the UK, so every award holder is an international student in UK terms
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: One-year taught master's degree only, at any eligible UK university; three different courses must be chosen and their eligibility checked in the Chevening course finder, with duplicate courses at the same university not permitted
official.description: Chevening Scholarships enable outstanding emerging leaders from all over the world to pursue one-year master's degrees in the UK; the awards are funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office and partner organisations so scholars can drive impact in areas of shared priority for the UK and their home countries.
official.program_type: UK Government international scholarship programme (FCDO) for one-year master's degrees
official.english_requirement: No English test score is required - the Chevening English language requirement was removed in 2020. The application form must still be completed in English or it is deemed ineligible, the interview is conducted in English, and applicants must meet their chosen university's own English requirements to secure an unconditional offer.

not_confirmed: a single central deadline (deadlines are set per country/territory page)
verification.notes: Every benefit and rule was read directly on chevening.org, including the 'What does a Chevening Scholarship cover?' FAQ and the eligibility, common errors and timeline guidance pages. Chevening publishes no monetary figure for the stipend - the FAQ states only that it depends on studying inside or outside London and is subject to annual review - so the amount is recorded as null rather than taken from any aggregator. Note also that the site's country pages show deadlines differing by country, with some already closed for the 2027-28 cycle.

applicant_utility.summary: Chevening pays tuition fees outright and adds a monthly stipend that differs inside and outside London, plus economy travel both ways, arrival and departure allowances, the visa fee and a travel top-up - but the scheme never publishes the stipend figure, so budget from UK university cost-of-living guidance rather than from any quoted number. Two hard gates catch most people out: the deadline is set by your own country page rather than centrally, and you must apply from your country of citizenship even if you live elsewhere. Work on the three university course choices immediately after submitting, because you need an unconditional offer from one of them by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Professionals with roughly two to eight years of post-degree work experience, a leadership track record and a credible plan to take those skills home afterwards.
application_readiness_checklist: Open your own country/territory page on chevening.org and note its exact closing time in UTC - do not rely on any general deadline date
Total your post-graduation work history as weeks multiplied by hours per week (typically 35-60 hours a week, 40-50 weeks a year) and confirm you clear 2,800 hours
Shortlist three different eligible one-year taught master's courses at different universities and verify each in the Chevening course finder before submitting
Write the four essay answers yourself, with concrete leadership and relationship-building examples, and keep proof that no AI tool was used
Line up two referees who know you professionally and send them the required letter format early, since Chevening will not contact them for you
If you are shortlisted, upload photo ID, your original degree certificate and both reference letters at least seven working days before the interview
common_rejection_risks: Applying from the wrong country - you must apply from your country of citizenship regardless of where you currently live
Work-experience hours that do not reach 2,800, or the same job entered twice, or unrealistic weekly hours - the total is calculated automatically from weeks and hours
Choosing three courses that are not eligible, or two courses at the same university, which cannot be considered
Any part of the application generated by AI or copied from elsewhere, including polished-looking essay text produced by a chatbot
Submitting the form in a language other than English, which makes the application ineligible outright
Missing your country's own deadline, since the online system locks after it and some countries close earlier than others
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published awards cover the scholar's tuition, living stipend, flights, visa fee, arrival and departure allowances and a travel top-up, so the main gaps are anything for accompanying family members, deposits or furniture for accommodation, extra baggage, and any costs your university or city imposes beyond the stipend. Because the stipend rate is never published, plan your budget against UK student cost-of-living figures and assume no top-up from Chevening.
document_audit: Only the official degree certificate issued by your university is accepted - transcripts are explicitly rejected, though no English translation is needed

Reference letters must be in English, addressed to the British embassy or high commission in your country, and include the referee's contact details, how long and in what capacity they have known you and when you last had regular contact
Letters in another language need the original plus a notarised English translation; unofficial translations are not accepted
Documents are not needed to submit, only after an interview invitation, but universities will need your transcripts and English evidence separately for their own admissions
alerts: For the 2027-28 cycle many country pages were already closed by 10 October 2026 while a few ran to 20 October 2026, so treat your country page as the only deadline
The unconditional offer deadline is 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027 - a late offer forfeits the award even after a successful interview
Employees, immediate relatives and recent former employees of the FCDO, British Council or partner universities are barred, and previous UK government-funded study makes you ineligible

The interview is conducted in English at a British embassy or high commission, and Chevening states that strong English skills are needed to write a competitive application even though no test score is required
Chevening does not endorse or work with anyone who charges for application help, and applying is free - treat paid 'guaranteed placement' offers as a red flag
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register in the online application system through your country page, pass the eligibility checker, submit the form with your three course choices, then wait for sifting, independent reading committees and an embassy interview before the final university offer check.
